caveats: PARTIAL: covers lecture 1 of 18. Do not cite this KB as covering CS336 as a whole. Lectures 2-18 - architectures, GPUs, kernels, parallelism, scaling laws, inference, evaluation, data, mid/post-training, RLVR, multimodality - have no transcripts and no wiki pages here.

Lecture 1 is an executable Python program (lecture_01.py), not a slide deck, so the written material was transcribed from source text exactly. That is not a lower grade than page-images for this lecture; there are no slides to have looked at.

Figures are the one gap. The lecture displays images via image() calls; raw/slides records each one at the point it appears, by path or URL, WITHOUT describing its contents, because the build read source text rather than rendered images. No claim in the wiki rests on a figure's contents.

Worked numeric values (compression ratios, token ids, BPE merge sequences, vocabulary sizes) do not appear in the lecture source - they are produced at runtime by @inspect annotations. The values in this KB were obtained by executing the lecture's own code verbatim, and raw/slides says so at the head of the tokenization section. They are reproducible, not recalled.

The half of CS336 taught by Tatsunori Hashimoto (lectures 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11, 15, 16) IS conventional PDF decks. Those are not transcribed here, and transcribing them would require page-images rather than source-text.

The transcript was copy-edited from auto-captions. The verbatim captions are kept alongside at raw/transcripts/original/. Two places where the captions are genuinely ambiguous are marked inline with [Ed:] notes rather than guessed.
